title: GEPA: Reflective Prompt Evolution Can Outperform Reinforcement Learning | alphaXiv
snippet: GEPA is a framework for optimizing any system with textual parameters against any evaluation metric. GEPA is an evolutionary optimizer, which uses reflection to evolve text components of complex systems.
claim: GEPA uses full execution traces including error messages and reasoning to identify and propose targeted prompt improvements without requiring dense reward signals.

topic: Execution trace analysis for skill feedback

title: GitHub - CerebrasResearch/gepa: Optimize prompts, code, and more with AI-powered Reflective Text Evolution
snippet: GEPA executes a selected candidate on a sampled minibatch of input queries, tracing the program's execution. From the execution traces, GEPA extracts the module's inputs, outputs, and reasoning, and calls a feedback function which returns a numeric score and text feedback including details about the evaluation.
claim: The reflective process uses LLM analysis of execution traces from failed and successful attempts to perform credit assignment and identify prompt improvements.

query: ACE Generator Reflector Curator loop AI self-improvement
title: Agentic Context Engineering: Evolving Contexts for Self-Improving Language Models
snippet: ACE works through a three-step loop: Generator runs the current task using the existing playbook, Reflector reviews the outcome and identifies what helped or hurt, and Curator/Mutator integrates updates into the playbook.
claim: The ACE framework uses a three-component loop where Generator executes, Reflector analyzes outcomes, and Curator integrates only actionable updates into the playbook.

topic: Continuous improvement feedback loops for AI agents

title: The Agent Improvement Loop Starts with a Trace
snippet: A trace captures the full execution of an agent run: every LLM call, every tool invocation, every retrieval step, every intermediate output, and the sequence of decisions connecting them. Reliable agents are built from a trace-centered improvement loop that begins with tracing and returns to tracing.
claim: Production traces and user feedback form the foundation of continuous improvement loops that verify fixes and enable controlled rollouts.

title: How to Build a Self-Improving AI Agent That Learns From Its Own Mistakes
snippet: A learning store is a persistent file or database the agent reads at the start of each run, where the agent writes lessons after identifying what went wrong, allowing it to read those lessons on the next run. When feedback immediately translates into learning or improvement activities, it closes the feedback loop and significantly boosts the value of performance management.
claim: A persistent learning store enables agents to read lessons from prior runs and write improvements after identifying failures, closing the feedback loop.

title: SkillAxe: Sharpening LLM-Authored Agent Skills Through Evaluation-Guided Self-Refinement
snippet: SkillAxe computes diagnostic evaluations without requiring task-specific labels or handcrafted reward functions, using LLMs as general-purpose judges.
claim: Skill evaluation can be automated using LLM-based judges to provide diagnostic feedback that drives iterative self-refinement without manual labels.

title: Building a Prompt Engineering Feedback Loop: The System That Made My AI Prompts 3x More Effective
snippet: For production systems, updating a template allows you to diff it against the previous version and measure whether outputs improved. Every API call should log the prompt version, the input variables, and a quality score (automated or manual). Additionally, A/B test template changes by running both versions on the same inputs for a week and comparing output quality before fully switching.
claim: Practical prompt improvement loops require versioning, quality metrics on each call, and A/B testing before rollout to measure whether changes actually improved outcomes.

topic: Agile retrospective as a review and improvement ceremony
query: agile ceremony retro review feedback system
title: The Ultimate Guide to Agile Retrospectives
snippet: An Agile retrospective is a short meeting where the team reflects on how they worked during the last sprint, with the goal to understand what went well, what didn't, and what small changes could make the next sprint smoother. Most Agile retrospectives follow a simple flow: set the stage, review what happened, generate insights, agree on a small set of improvement actions, and close with clear owners and next steps.
claim: Agile retrospectives use a structured flow of review, insight generation, and bounded improvement actions with clear ownership and followup.
